messages.subject: NAs in setup_date
parts:
Hi. I was wondering if you could help me. 

I am currently working on a database that unfortunately has NAs on the setup_data and retrieval date. For some reason those dates and times were not recorded. Now I am trying to do the data frame for the camera operations to be able to do the occupancy matrix. However, I get this error at the bottom. My stations had two cameras each. 

> carmelita_camop <- cameraOperation(CTtable = camtrapsCarmelita, #file
+                                    stationCol = "Station",
+                                    cameraCol = "CameraID", 
+                                    byCamera = TRUE,
+                                    setupCol = "Setup_date",
+                                    retrievalCol = "Retrieval_date",
+                                    writecsv = FALSE,
+                                    hasProblems = FALSE,
+                                    dateFormat = "%Y-%m-%d",
+                                    camerasIndependent = FALSE)
Error in cameraOperation(CTtable = camtrapsCarmelita, stationCol = "Station",  : 
  there are NAs in setupCol

Is there a way to get around this error so I can do the camera operation table and occupancy matrix (detectionHistory)? 

Thank you!! 

Gabby

messages.author: 0b86ca0cb4b615b0
messages.subject: Re: NAs in setup_date
parts:
Dear Gabriella,
the NA basically means you don't know when it was set up / retrieved. In other words, there is no information to base the calculation of trap effort on.  Hence camtrapR insists on not having NAs in these fields.

You have 2 possibilites: 
1) In the absence of any other information, you may enter the dates of the first / last image taken at that station (from the record table) into the setup / retrieval columns. That would be a conservative and safe way. Or any other educated guess of a date.
2) remove these cameras

But be aware that the camera operation matrix and subsequently the detection matrix / effort matrix depend on the setup / retrieval dates. For example, if the setup date you enter is too early, you may end up with lots of 0s in the detection matrix and high values in the effort matrix for those days, which may bias computation of detection probabilities. 
If you remove stations, you will lose data. So if possible, I'd suggest to go with option 1.

Best regards,
Jürgen
